as_told.title: Brown at Martin Corporation the year Skunkworks was formed

plain: The inventor Thomas Townsend Brown, who believed electricity could affect gravity, was suddenly let go by the Navy in 1942 'with no explanation, despite strong performance', and then went to the aircraft maker Martin in the same year that Skunk Works, the secret aircraft design shop led by the engineer Kelly Johnson, was formed in Burbank. Michels says this himself, reading from Brown's naval records and from his FBI file of 1942 and 1943; once he gives the year as '1942 or three', and in two versions he does not mention the firing at all. He tells it to suggest that Brown's work was being moved to secret aircraft projects, though by his own account the records show the firing and the new job, and say nothing about why.
